title: Nonprofit Accounting - FASB Standards
learning_objectives: Account for donated services and assets

overview.standard_setter: FASB (same as for-profit, but special nonprofit guidance)
overview.key_difference: Focus on NET ASSETS (not equity), classified by donor restrictions
overview.no_fund_accounting: Unlike government, nonprofits don't use fund accounting (use single entity approach)

required_statements.name: Statement of Financial Position
required_statements.key_section: Net assets (with donor restrictions, without donor restrictions)

required_statements.name: Statement of Activities
required_statements.shows: Changes in net assets by class, revenues and expenses

required_statements.name: Statement of Functional Expenses
required_statements.shows: Expenses by function (program, management, fundraising) AND nature (salaries, rent, etc.)

two_classes.description: No donor-imposed restrictions (may have board designations, but those don't create restrictions)
two_classes.examples: Unrestricted contributions, earned revenues, board-designated funds

two_classes.formerly: Temporarily restricted and permanently restricted (combined under ASU 2016-14)

net_asset_classifications.release_from_restrictions: When purpose accomplished or time passed, reclassify from 'with restrictions' to 'without restrictions'

contributions.definition: Unconditional transfer of cash or other assets (or settlement of liabilities) to nonprofit
contributions.recognition: Revenue when RECEIVED or UNCONDITIONALLY PROMISED

conditional_vs_unconditional.unconditional_promise: Recognize immediately as contribution revenue and receivable
conditional_vs_unconditional.conditional_promise: Do NOT recognize until condition substantially met
conditional_vs_unconditional.example_conditional: Donor promises $100K if nonprofit raises matching $100K from others. Conditional - recognize when match achieved.
conditional_vs_unconditional.example_unconditional: Donor promises $100K payable in 3 years. Unconditional - recognize immediately at PV.

classification: If no donor restriction → Without donor restrictions
If purpose or time restriction → With donor restrictions
contributions.multiyear_pledges: Record at PRESENT VALUE, recognize contribution discount as revenue over time

purpose_restriction.initial:
DR Cash/Pledge Receivable
   CR Contribution Revenue - With Restrictions
purpose_restriction.when_spent_on_purpose:
DR Net Assets Released - With Restrictions (deduction in 'with' column)
   CR Net Assets Released - Without Restrictions (addition in 'without' column)

perpetual_endowment.earnings: May be with or without restrictions depending on donor specification

donated_services.recognition_criteria: Recognize as contribution revenue and expense if EITHER:
criteria: Create or enhance nonfinancial assets (e.g., construction services), OR
Require specialized skills + provided by individuals possessing those skills + would typically need to be purchased if not donated
donated_services.journal_entry:
DR Expense (or Asset if creating asset)
   CR Contribution Revenue - Donated Services

donated_assets.noncash: Contribution revenue at FAIR VALUE of asset received
donated_assets.example: Donor gives land (FV $200K). DR Land $200K, CR Contribution Revenue $200K (classify per restrictions)

categories.examples: Fundraising events, donor cultivation, grant writing

functional_expense_classification.allocation: Expenses serving multiple functions must be allocated using reasonable basis
functional_expense_classification.presentation: Statement of Functional Expenses shows expenses by BOTH function and nature (matrix format)

special_events.accounting: Separate direct costs from contribution portion

gross_method.description: Report gross revenues and gross expenses
gross_method.example: Gala raises $100K, costs $30K. Report $100K revenue, $30K fundraising expense. Net = $70K.

net_method.description: Report only contribution portion as revenue, direct costs as reduction
net_method.example: Contribution portion $70K shown as revenue. May show $100K gross with $30K offsetting.

special_events.exchange_transactions: If attendees receive commensurate value (e.g., dinner worth ticket price), that portion is exchange transaction, not contribution

statement_of_activities_format.bottom_line: Change in net assets for each class

endowments.true_endowment: Donor-imposed perpetual restriction on principal. Only earnings may be spent (per donor or policy).
endowments.board_designated_endowment: Board sets aside funds to function as endowment. Classified as WITHOUT donor restrictions (board can change designation).
endowments.investment_returns: Classify based on donor restriction on endowment. If true endowment with no restriction on earnings, earnings are without restrictions.

cpa_exam_strategies.net_assets: Two classes: Without restrictions and With restrictions. Release when purpose/time met.
cpa_exam_strategies.conditional_vs_unconditional: Conditional (barrier, right of return) = don't recognize until met. Unconditional = recognize immediately (even if future payment).
cpa_exam_strategies.donated_services: Recognize if create/enhance assets OR specialized skill typically purchased. Fair value.
cpa_exam_strategies.functional_expenses: Program, management, fundraising. Must allocate shared expenses.
cpa_exam_strategies.most_tested: Net asset classification, conditional promises, donated services recognition.

key_points: Two net asset classes: Without donor restrictions, With donor restrictions
Contributions: Recognize when received or unconditionally promised
Conditional promises: Don't recognize until condition substantially met
Release restrictions when purpose accomplished or time passed
Donated services: Recognize if specialized + typically purchased, or create/enhance assets
Functional expenses: Program, management and general, fundraising
Endowments: True (perpetual restriction) vs. board-designated (no restriction)
Statement of Functional Expenses required for VHWOs
